title: Learned code distance regularizer for Mirror bank
hypothesis: At a fixed 8-bit address budget, a development-optimized minimum-distance codebook will reduce held-out noisy logical-function misrouting relative to random code assignments without increasing serialized codebook bytes.
physical_object: shared decoder with 32 logical functions and fixed 8-bit addresses
mirror_coordinate: learned binary codeword trained/selected for inter-function distance

task.type: synthetic address transmission with independent bit flips

development.allowed: choose codebook from predeclared random candidate pool by maximum minimum distance; no fresh-dependent selection

success_gate: At p=.1, optimized code reduces misroute rate >=25% versus random 8-bit codes at equal payload bytes, with 100% noiseless accuracy.
failure_gate: No noise robustness gain at equal bytes, or code separation only improves at additional address bits.
boundaries: This tests codebook selection, not neural router training or task quality.
Code distance is not functional capacity.

amendment_A1.reason: The initial random-code control accidentally allowed duplicate codewords, producing <100% noiseless accuracy and invalidating comparison to selected codebooks. A0 is preserved as exploratory.
amendment_A1.change: Require unique codewords for all random/optimized codebooks; no gate change.
